math_proof: At a straight track face, the wheel center is offset by perpendicular distance r. At a convex crest it can pivot on the crest so its center follows a circle of radius r about that crest. At a concave V, before the apex can be reached the wheel touches both faces; its center is the intersection of the two face-offset lines. It then leaves the incoming straight center path and follows the outgoing straight path with a sharp switch at that intersection. A smooth arc centered on the valley vertex would intersect one face or lose the required contact relation, so A is wrong. Only E has rounded crests and sharp valleys. Original track and proposed loci, wheel size, all paths, labels and arrowheads are untouched except for existing stroke colors/width2. The red native bend consists of 30 already-existing straight sampling fragments; no point or path has been added. This design does not retest or alter the earlier B PNG/preset.
